name: Yalova
title: Yalova Shipyard Thickness Gauging | Altınova UTM
description: Thickness gauging at the Yalova and Altınova shipyards: in-dock and pre-docking UTM for renewal survey steel planning, hull structure and piping checks.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement at the Altınova Shipyards, Yalova
intro: Yalova's Altınova shipyard zone, on the southern shore of the Sea of Marmara near the mouth of the Gulf of Izmit, is a concentrated cluster of Turkish shipyards for newbuilding, conversion and repair. Ships arrive here for docking, renewal surveys and steel renewal, and the gauging plan decides how quickly the yard can start on the steel. We mobilise a team from India for thickness measurement in Yalova, timed to the docking and coordinated with the yard and the superintendent.

highlights.p: In-dock gauging at Altınova is planned around the docking programme: bottom and side shell while the ship is dry, tanks as they are cleaned and certified, with readings passed to the yard as each area is finished.
Readings taken before the ship arrives, at anchor off Yalova or at its last cargo port in the Marmara, let the yard order plate and plan staging and labour before the ship is opened up.
Altınova lies across the water from Tuzla and close to the Kocaeli terminals, so jobs in the Yalova yards can be combined with work at Tuzla or in the Gulf of Izmit within one mobilisation.

port.h: Yalova and the Altınova shipyard zone
p: Yalova is a province on the southern shore of the Sea of Marmara, across the water from Istanbul and linked to it by fast ferries and, by road, through the Osmangazi Bridge over the Gulf of Izmit. Its maritime identity rests on shipbuilding rather than cargo. The Altınova shipyard zone, east of the city near the entrance to the gulf, has developed into a cluster of yards building and repairing ships for Turkish and international owners, with floating docks, building berths and outfitting quays side by side.

The yards at Altınova build tugs, ferries, chemical and product tankers, offshore and fishing vessels and other specialised ships, and many of them also take ships for docking, repair and conversion. Yalova ship repair brings in bulk carriers, tankers, general cargo ships and ro-ro vessels from owners in Turkey, Greece, the Black Sea countries and beyond, often for renewal surveys where steel renewal is expected. Because the yards are a short passage from the Istanbul anchorages and the Kocaeli terminals, ships can come in from their last cargo port in the Marmara with little deviation, and superintendents from Istanbul can attend daily. Dry docking in Yalova is normally planned well ahead, which leaves time to plan the gauging properly too.

Inspection demand in Yalova is defined by the yard stay. Ships are here specifically to be docked and repaired, so the gauging extent is often the full extent the survey in hand requires, and its timing matters: readings that arrive late hold up steel renewal, staging and the undocking date. For older ships at their third or fourth renewal survey, gauging and steel renewal are often the critical path of the whole docking, and the superintendent needs measured data early to control it. Conversion projects add their own needs, such as establishing the condition of structure that will be reused in the converted ship.

facilities.h: Where we gauge in the Yalova yards
p: Most work is in floating docks and at the repair quays of the Altınova yards, under each yard's safety, permit and access rules. In dock, we measure bottom plating, bilge, side shell and sea chests while the hull is dry and staging or access platforms are in place, and gauge cargo holds, ballast tanks and cargo tanks as they are cleaned, gas-freed and certified. Alongside, before or after docking, the focus shifts to decks, hatch covers, internal structure and piping systems, which can be reached without holding up the dock.

Pre-docking gauging is done at anchor off Yalova or at the ship's last port, so that the yard receives a steel renewal estimate before the docking date. After steel renewal, we can re-gauge adjacent plating that was close to the renewal limit, so the superintendent has a complete record to put before the attending class surveyor. Each yard runs its own gate and permit procedures, which the ship's agent and the yard's project manager arrange before the team arrives. In-dock thickness gauging and the post-renewal checks go into one report, so the surveyor sees the whole picture rather than two partial ones.
list: Floating docks at the Altınova yards — bottom, bilge, side shell and sea chest gauging while the ship is dry during the renewal or docking survey
Repair quays in the yard zone — gauging of holds, tanks, decks, hatch covers and piping before and after docking
Anchorage off Yalova — pre-docking gauging on ships waiting for a dock, giving the yard a steel estimate before arrival
Conversion berths — condition gauging of existing structure to be retained in conversion projects, marked against the conversion drawings
Tuzla yards and Kocaeli terminals nearby — combined programmes across the eastern Marmara within one mobilisation

context.h: Regulation and market context for Turkish shipyards
p: Yalova lies on the Sea of Marmara, inside the Mediterranean SOx ECA in force since 1 May 2025, and Turkey participates in both the Mediterranean MoU and the Black Sea MoU on port state control. For a ship in a Yalova dock, the regulatory work is mostly class and flag: renewal and docking surveys, the ESP requirements for oil tankers, chemical tankers and bulk carriers, and any port state control deficiencies carried in from previous ports. A docking is also the natural time to deal with scrubber wash-water and overboard piping, which is easiest to repair at the shell connections with the ship dry.

The market around the yards is competitive and international. Turkish shipyards compete for European and regional repair work with yards in the Black Sea, the Mediterranean and the Middle East, and schedule reliability is a central factor in choosing between them. That puts weight on early, organised gauging: a yard can only commit to an undocking date once it knows the steel scope, and owners who bring measured readings to the discussion are better placed to agree a realistic programme. Ships with EU owners or trading to EU ports also carry EU ETS and FuelEU obligations on those voyages.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Yalova
jobs.p: Nearly all Yalova jobs are linked to a docking. A superintendent sends the survey status and previous thickness reports, we agree a gauging plan with the yard's project manager, and the team arrives for pre-docking readings or for the first days of the docking. Thickness measurement in Yalova is therefore planned in detail before travel, not worked out on arrival.
list: Third renewal survey gauging on a chemical tanker in an Altınova floating dock, measuring bottom and side shell while dry and cargo and ballast tanks as they are certified.
Pre-docking gauging on a Handysize bulk carrier at anchor off Yalova, with hold frames, hopper plating and topside tanks measured so the yard can order steel before docking.
Gauging of existing structure on a ship coming in for conversion, to confirm which plating and stiffeners can be reused in the new arrangement.
Re-gauging of plating adjacent to renewed areas on a general cargo ship after steel renewal, completing the record for the attending surveyor.
Sea water, ballast and fire main piping inspection on a ro-ro ship during its docking, ahead of the yard's pipe renewal decisions.

logistics: The team flies into Istanbul, usually Sabiha Gökçen Airport, and reaches Yalova by road over the Osmangazi Bridge or by fast ferry from Istanbul. Each yard in the Altınova zone has its own gate procedures, so access is arranged through the yard's project manager and the ship's agent, with crew lists, technician certificates and equipment details sent in advance; launches for anchorage work are booked by the agent. Turkish visas are required for technicians travelling from India, so we apply once the docking date is set and ask to be told at once if the yard moves the slot.

faqs.q: When should gauging start for a docking at Altınova?
faqs.a: Ideally before the ship arrives. Pre-docking gauging at anchor or at the last cargo port gives the yard a steel estimate before docking. Where that is not possible, we aim to start in the first days in dock with the areas most likely to need renewal, so steel ordering is not held up while the rest of the ship is measured.

faqs.q: Can you work within the yard's own schedule and permits?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Altınova yard runs its own permit-to-work, gas-free certification and access procedures, and we follow them. We agree a gauging sequence with the yard's project manager so that staging, cleaning and gas-freeing are done in the order that suits both the measurement and the steelwork, and so the dock is not kept waiting on readings.

faqs.q: Do you measure structure on ships coming to Yalova for conversion?
faqs.a: Yes. In a conversion, the owner needs to know which existing structure can be kept. We gauge plating and stiffeners in the areas to be retained or modified, mark readings against the conversion drawings, and identify where wastage would make reuse impractical, so the design and steel quantities rest on measured data.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover yards in Yalova and Tuzla?
faqs.a: Yes. The two shipyard areas face each other across the eastern Marmara and are linked by road and ferry. If you have ships docking in both within a short period, we plan a single mobilisation with a visa period that covers both, and sequence the jobs around each yard's docking dates.
